sanskrit: sahṛdayaṃ sāṃmanasyam avidveṣaṃ kṛṇomi vaḥ | anyo anyam abhi haryata vatsaṃ jātam ivāghnyā ||
english: I make for you concord of heart, unity of mind, freedom from enmity. Love one another as a newly-born calf is loved by the cow that may not be slain.

sanskrit: anuvrataḥ pituḥ putro mātrā bhavatu savrataḥ | jāyā patye madhumatīṃ vācaṃ vadatu śantivām ||
english: Let the son be obedient in vow to his father, of one vow with his mother. Let the wife speak to her husband words that are honey-sweet, full of peace.

sanskrit: mā bhrātā bhrātaraṃ dvikṣan mā svasāram uta svasā | samyañcaḥ savratā bhūtvā vācaṃ vadata bhadrayā ||
english: Let not brother hate brother, nor sister hate sister. Being harmonious, of one vow, speak ye words that are auspicious.

sanskrit: yena devā na viyanti no ca vidviṣate mithaḥ | tat kṛṇmo brahma vo gṛhe saṃjñānaṃ puruṣebhyaḥ ||
english: By that which the gods do not separate, nor bear mutual hatred for one another — that sacred formula we make operative in your house: concord among the people thereof.

sanskrit: jyāyasvantaś cittino mā vi yauṣṭa saṃrādhayantaḥ sadhurāś carantaḥ | anyo anyasmai valgu vadanta eta samagrā stha sadhrīcīnāḥ ||
english: You who are endowed with vigour and understanding — be not separated; accomplishing your aims, going together on the same track. Speaking pleasant words to one another, come together; be whole, united in a common direction.

sanskrit: samānī prapā saha vo 'nnabhāgaḥ samāne yoktre saha vo yunajmi | samyañco 'gniṃ saparyata- -arā nābhim ivābhitaḥ ||
english: Common is your drinking-trough, common is your share of food; together I yoke you in a common bond. Tending Agni in harmony, as spokes surround a hub.

sanskrit: yena devā haviṣā yajatrā apa pāpmānam aghnata | krodhaṃ manyum anṛtaṃ bhāmaṃ duruktam abhiśocanam āre yakṣmaṃ ni dadhmasi ||
english: By the oblation with which the adorable gods drove away evil — anger, wrath, falsehood, fury, ill-speech, and consuming grief — far off we lay down disease.

sanskrit: sadhrīcīnān vaḥ saṃmanasaḥ kṛṇomy ekaśnuṣṭīn saṃvananena saṃhṛdaḥ | devā ived amṛtaṃ rakṣamāṇāḥ sāyaṃprātaḥ susamitir vo astu ||
english: I make you united in direction, of one mind, eating together, won over by the charm and joined in heart. Like the gods guarding immortality, may your assembly be well-composed morning and evening.

sanskrit: paro 'pehi paraś cara paras tarda parastaram | agner vātasya dhrājyā apa bādhe ahaṃ tvām ||
english: Away, begone! Move afar! Pierce thou yet farther still! By the swift dart of Agni and Vāyu I drive thee away.

sanskrit: udakasyedam ayanaṃ vātasyedaṃ nibhañjanam | agner dhūmasyāyaṃ panthā neha tardāyanaṃ tava ||
english: This is the course of water; this is the breaking-place of the wind; this is the path of Agni's smoke — here is no passage for thee, O wood-borer.

sanskrit: pari tvā kṛṣṇavartanir agnir dhūmenārciṣā | sa tvaṃ tarda paraś cara- -anyat tarddhi tṛṇaṃ yavāt ||
english: Agni of the black track encircles thee with smoke and flame. Thou, O wood-borer, move away! Pierce something else — pierce the grass, spare the barley.

sanskrit: ye tardā asureṣitā devebhir iṣitāś ca ye | sarvāṃs tān brahmaṇā vayaṃ śalabhāñ jambhayāmasi ||
english: Those wood-borers that are impelled by the Asuras, and those impelled by the gods — all of them together with the locusts we crush by the power of brahman.

sanskrit: śalabhasya śalabhyās tardasyo patatriṇaḥ | agner vātasya dhrājyā- -api nahyāma āsyam ||
english: Of the locust, of the female locust, of the wood-borer, of every flying creature — with the swift dart of Agni and Vāyu we seal shut the mouth.

sanskrit: idaṃ yad gavi bheṣajaṃ viśvād rūpāt samābhṛtam | ākhor ghuṇasya tardasya teṣāṃ snāvnāpi nahyata ||
english: This remedy gathered from the cow, assembled from every form — with its sinew-cord do we bind the mouths of the mouse, the ghuṇa-grub, and the wood-borer.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭā tvam asi gandhena- -oṣadhir ghuṇajambhanī | ākhor ghuṇasya jātāni tāni jambhaya tejasā ||
english: Thou art perceived by thy fragrance, O herb that crushes the ghuṇa-grub. Crush with thy fiery power all the species of the mouse and the ghuṇa-grub.

sanskrit: tūlaṃ tardas tṛṇasyāttu mūlam ākhur dhiyeṣitaḥ | atho vṛkṣasya phalgu yad ghuṇā adantu mā yavam ||
english: Let the wood-borer eat the pith of the grass, let the mouse urged by its instinct eat the root; and let the ghuṇa-grubs eat the pithy part of the tree — but let them not eat the barley.

sanskrit: dyauś ca naḥ pitā pṛthivī ca mātā- -agniś ca nṛcakṣā jātavedāḥ | te takmānam adharāñcaṃ nyañcaṃ daśāhnam asyantv adhi dūram asmat ||
english: Heaven is our father and Earth our mother; Agni, the all-seeing Jātavedas, watches over men. May they hurl the fever-demon downward, prostrate, ten-day-bound, far away from us.

sanskrit: takman yaṃ te kṣetrabhāgam apābhajaṃ pṛthivyāḥ pūrve ardhe | atihāya tam atha no hinassi grāhiḥ kila tvā grahīṣyati kilāsaśīrṣaḥ ||
english: O Takmán, having allotted thee thy territory in the eastern half of the earth — passing beyond that, thou dost afflict us. Seizure shall surely seize thee — the white-headed seizure.

sanskrit: takman parvatā ime himavantaḥ somapṛṣṭhāḥ | vātaṃ dūtaṃ bhiṣajaṃ no akran naśyeto maraṭām̐ abhi ||
english: O Takmán, yonder are these snow-capped mountains, the Himavants, their ridges bright with soma. They have made the wind our messenger and healer — vanish hence, away to the Muñjavaṭ tribes!

sanskrit: na tvā striyaḥ kāmayante na pumāṃsaḥ katame cana | neha takmakāmyā- -alpo roditi no mahān ||
english: Women do not desire thee, nor do any men whatsoever. Here there is no one longing for the fever — neither the small cries for thee nor the great.

sanskrit: mā no hiṃsīr mahato mā hiṃsīr mahyas tvam | kumārān babhro mā hiṃsīr mā no hiṃsīḥ kumāryaḥ ||
english: Harm not the great ones, harm not thou the elder men. O tawny one, harm not the boys; harm not our girls.

sanskrit: yaḥ sākam utpātayasi balāsaṃ kāsam udrajam | bhīmās te takman hetayas tābhi ṣma pari vṛṅdhi naḥ ||
english: Thou who dost at once send flying balāsa, cough, and udraja — dreadful are thy shafts, O Takmán; with them do thou spare us!

sanskrit: anyakṣetre na ramate sahasrākṣo 'martyaḥ | abhūd u prārthas takmā sa u no mṛḍayiṣyati ||
english: The thousand-eyed immortal one takes no pleasure in another's domain. The fever-demon Takmán has indeed been besought — he will be gracious to us.

sanskrit: takman na ta ihāśvā na gāvo neha te gṛhāḥ | śakambharasya muṣṭihā punar gaccha mahāvṛṣān ||
english: O Takmán, thou hast no horses here, no cattle, no dwellings here. O crusher of Śakambhara, go back to the great mountain ranges!
